$comment: example.journey.json — a worked example of the journey shape, shipped WITH the engine.
Two jobs. First, journey-runner.selftest.js falls back to this file when a project has
no journeys/ of its own, so the instrument that proves the assertions can fail is itself
runnable on day one instead of dying ENOENT before its first check.
Second, it is the reference for the shape — in particular for rung 4, where the three
claims are easy to confuse. They are NOT interchangeable:
delta          something was saved.
assocMustBeSet something was saved WITH its association filled in.
mustPointAt    ...and that association points at the RIGHT row.
Set-ness is not correctness. A journey that stops at delta passes over a record that
saved with a null link, and one that stops at assocMustBeSet passes over a record
linked to the wrong parent. Both read as green.
scope is MANDATORY whenever assocMustBeSet or mustPointAt is present: without a
watermark the query grades every row in the table, including rows that predate the run,
so a single good historical row carries the assertion. A data block that carries
assocMustBeSet with no scope must be reported [WEAK EVIDENCE], never silently accepted.
Names below are placeholders. Replace <Module>/<Entity>/<Widget>/<Microflow> with your own.
Every key here is one journey-runner.js reads (examples/validate-journeys.js reports 0
problems on this file). The field-by-field tour is skills/journey-examples.md.
Add "persona": "<TEST_USER>" when the journey proves one role's access path — a run signed in as anyone else records the journey INVALID and does not walk it.
title: Example — open the overview, submit the form, see the row on its parent

seeds.name: parentKey
seeds.$comment: Referenced later as {{parentKey}}. Seeds are the only values a step may assume exist; they are read from the live DB, never hardcoded. Every OQL column is aliased.
seeds.sql: SELECT p.<KeyAttribute> AS k FROM <Module>.<Parent> AS p LIMIT 1

steps.name: Open the overview and see the seeded row
steps.$comment: rung 1 landing guard + rung 2 what the screen says. Without the guard an assertion grades the PREVIOUS page.

steps.name: Submit the form
steps.$comment: rung 3 ordered spans, rung 4 data effects. A capture with zero spans is a fault, never a pass — [].every() is true. A step whose only proof is that something did NOT run declares mustNotFire alone (plus spans.liveness); see journey-examples.md.

mustNotFire: <Microflow that must not run, e.g. a delete>

oql.label: the new row exists and is not a draft
oql.sql: SELECT COUNT(e.ID) AS n FROM <Module>.<Entity> AS e WHERE e.<Status> != 'Draft'

outcome.$comment: rung 5. The thing the user actually came for, asserted once, in their terms.
outcome.label: the parent shows the submitted row
outcome.sql: SELECT COUNT(e.ID) AS n FROM <Module>.<Entity> AS e WHERE e/<Module>.<Entity>_<Parent>/<Module>.<Parent>/<KeyAttribute> = '{{parentKey}}'
